newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Arctic rejects gender-equal legislature.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Arctic rejects gender-equal legislature.

text.p: Voters in Canada's remote eastern Arctic defeated a proposal that would have made their legislature the world's first to require an equal number of men and women, final results showed on Tuesday.

Fifty-seven percent of voters in the sparsely populated region, which will become a separate Canadian territory called Nunavut in 1999, voted against the idea in a plebiscite on Monday. The vast eastern Arctic, which spans three time zones and extends to the North Pole, is home to just 25,000 people, many of them Inuit or Eskimo.
The plebiscite marked the end of a month-long debate in churches and gymnasiums in a dozen remote northern communities. Just 39 percent of 12,000 eligible cast ballots.

The controversial idea for "gender parity" in the legislature was put forward two years ago by a commission overseeing the creation of the new territory. Some of the most outspoken critics of the idea were women.

Some female leaders including the territorial minister responsible for women's equality said the measure would have amounted to a quota system. They wanted the chance to defeat male candidates on their own merits.
"It's a relief to know that this kind of consensus is coming from the people and not being dictated to them," Theresie Tungalik, a vocal opponent, said of the majority vote against the plan.

Supporters argued the idea would have ensured balanced representation of men and women in the legislature. If it had been approved voters would have cast two ballots in an upcoming election for Nunavut's first legislative assembly -- one from a list of male candidates and one from a list of female candidates.
"People find it hard to accept a new idea and the uncertainty about how it's going to work," Jose Kusugak, an Inuit leader and supporter of the proposal, said.

Women make up just over half of Nunavut's population but are dramatically under-represented in the current legislative assembly for the Northwest Territories in Yellowknife. Just two of 24 seats are held by women. Nunavut is being formed by splitting the Northwest Territories.
